items.title: Q1 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem: Which of the following is not matched correctly?
options: Ira De: The Hunt and Other Poems
Margaret Chatterjee: The Spring and the Spectacle
Tapati Mookerji: The Golden Road to Samerkhand
items.explanation: Tilottama Rajan is an eminent literary theorist best known for works like Dark Interpreter (1980), not Poems of Govindagraj. Govindagraj was the pen name of Marathi poet and dramatist Ram Ganesh Gadkari (1885–1919), whose poems were translated into English by Harold M. Patwardhan and Ganesh L. Chandavarkar. Ira De, Margaret Chatterjee, and Tapati Mookerji were all mid-20th-century Indian English women poets published by P. Lal's Writers Workshop.

items.title: Q2 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem: Who amongst the following was not a member of the Bloomsbury Group?
items.explanation: The Bloomsbury Group was an influential early 20th-century circle of English writers and intellectuals that included Virginia Woolf, E. M. Forster, Lytton Strachey, Clive Bell, Vanessa Bell, and John Maynard Keynes. W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet and playwright prominent in the Irish Literary Revival and the Rhymers' Club, not Bloomsbury.

items.title: Q4 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories and Pedagogy
items.stem: Functional Communicative Approach in English Language Teaching is in opposition to the:
items.explanation: The Functional-Communicative Approach (CLT) developed in direct opposition to the Structural Approach and audio-lingualism. While the Structural Approach prioritized mechanical drills and rigid grammatical habits, CLT emphasizes communicative competence and authentic, functional language use in real-life contexts.

items.title: Q5 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Arrange the following steps of ‘Decision making’ in the research process:
A. The choice of a research topic or theme.
B. Data collection
C. Analysis and interpretation of data.
D. Formulating the research problem.
E. Conceptualization and operationalization.
items.explanation: In standard research methodology, decision making proceeds systematically: selecting the broad research topic or theme (A), formulating and defining the research problem (D), conceptualizing and operationalizing key variables (E), collecting relevant empirical data (B), and analyzing and interpreting the collected data (C). This yields the sequence A -> D -> E -> B -> C.

items.title: Q6 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Renaissance, Elizabethan & Jacobean Age · Unit I: Drama
items.stem: Which among the following does not fall in the category of a Revenge Tragedy?
items.explanation: Shakespeare's Cymbeline (c. 1611) is a late romance or tragicomedy centered on pastoral disguise, forgiveness, and family reconciliation. In contrast, Thomas Kyd's The Spanish Tragedy, Christopher Marlowe's The Jew of Malta, and Shakespeare's Hamlet are definitive Elizabethan and Jacobean revenge tragedies driven by blood retribution.

items.title: Q8 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem:
Which of the given statements are correct?
A. Omprakash Valmiki’s Joothan is a novel.
B. Joothan represents the Dalit Valmiki community in critical light.
C. Joothan enumerates the difficulties of being a Dalit in independent India.
D. Joothan was translated into English by Arun Prabha Das.
E. Joothan critiques the upper castes.
items.explanation: Statements B, C, and E are correct: Joothan documents the struggles and internal conditions of the sweeper community, highlights systemic caste humiliation in post-independence India, and delivers a fierce critique of upper-caste hegemony. Statement A is false because Joothan is an autobiographical memoir, not a novel, and statement D is false because it was translated into English by Arun Prabha Mukherjee (not Arun Prabha Das).

items.title: Q9 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem:
From the statements given below, what is true about the Gothic Novel?
A. It appeared in 14th Century American Literature.
B. It often uses the medieval form of architecture as setting.
C. It is a form of baroque art.
D. It represents a style of mosaic and fresco wall painting.
E. It aims at evoking chilling terror by exploiting mystery and a variety of horrors.
items.explanation: Statements B and E are true: Gothic novels characteristically set their plots in medieval ruins, castles, and monasteries, aiming to evoke terror, dread, and suspense through the supernatural and mysterious. Statement A is false because the Gothic genre began in 18th-century England with Horace Walpole's The Castle of Otranto (1764), while C and D confuse literary Gothicism with unrelated visual arts.

items.title: Q10 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: What is ‘Practical Criticism’?
options: The close analysis of literary texts in such a way as to bring out their political meaning.
A movement which wished to make literary criticism more relevant.
The close analysis of poems without taking account of any external information.
items.explanation: Practical Criticism refers to the method established by I. A. Richards in his 1929 book Practical Criticism, where Cambridge students were asked to analyze poems presented without author names, titles, or dates. This pioneered close, text-centered reading that evaluates poetic language purely on its own merits without relying on external biographical or historical context.

items.title: Q11 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: “There is nothing outside the text” is a statement by:
items.explanation: The aphorism "Il n'y a pas de hors-texte" (translated as "There is nothing outside the text" or "There is no outside-text") was formulated by French philosopher Jacques Derrida in Of Grammatology (1967). Derrida argued that human understanding of reality is always mediated through signs, language, and contextual interpretation rather than unmediated presence.

items.title: Q12 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Who has written The Life Divine?
items.explanation: The Life Divine (1939–1940) is Sri Aurobindo's principal philosophical work, in which he articulates his theory of spiritual evolution, the ascent of human consciousness toward the Supermind, and the realization of divine life on earth.

items.title: Q13 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VI: English in India: History, Evolution and Futures

B. Alfred W. Crosby : “Unhiding the Hidden”
C. Paul Carter : “Naming Place”
D. Graham Huggan: “Ecological Imperialism”
E. Thomas B Macaulay : “Minutes on Indian Education”
items.explanation: Barbara Christian published the landmark Black feminist essay "The Race for Theory" in 1987 (A); Paul Carter authored "Naming Place" in his spatial history The Road to Botany Bay (1987) (C); and Thomas Babington Macaulay presented his historic "Minute on Indian Education" in 1835 (E). B and D are mismatched because Ecological Imperialism (1986) was authored by Alfred W. Crosby, while "Unhiding the Hidden" is an essay by Robert Kroetsch.

items.title: Q14 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: The line “Thou still unravished bride of quietness” presents which of the following rhetorical figures?
items.explanation: An apostrophe is a figure of speech in which a speaker directly addresses an absent person, personified quality, or inanimate object. In the famous opening line of John Keats's "Ode on a Grecian Urn" (1819), the speaker uses an apostrophe to address the silent marble urn as the "still unravished bride of quietness."

items.title: Q15 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem:
Identify the correct statements concerning the respective genre:
A. An epistle is a literary genre in the form of letter.
B. Epigraph is an inscription on funeral monument.
C. Epigram is a short, pithy poem wittily expressed.
D. Epitaph is a formal statement in the beginning of a literary work
E. Epyllion is a short poem in the meter of an epic poetry.
items.explanation: Statements A, C, and E are correct: an epistle is a literary composition in the form of a letter, an epigram is a concise and witty statement or poem, and an epyllion is a brief narrative poem composed in epic meter. Statements B and D have their definitions reversed: an epigraph is an introductory quotation at the beginning of a literary work, whereas an epitaph is an inscription on a tombstone or funeral monument.

items.explanation: Mary Shelley's major novels include Frankenstein (1818), Valperga (1823), The Last Man (1826), Lodore (1835), and Falkner (1837). The Lost Woman is not a novel by Mary Shelley (Willa Cather wrote A Lost Lady).

Naik's A History of Indian English Literature (1982), Gauri Viswanathan's Masks of Conquest (1989), G. N. Devy's After Amnesia (1992), and Harish Trivedi's Colonial Transactions (1993). This yields the sequence B -> D -> A -> C -> E.

items.title: Q19 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Identify the one who was not a ‘New Critic’:
items.explanation: Allen Tate, Robert Penn Warren, and Cleanth Brooks were prominent figures of American New Criticism who championed formalist close reading and textual autonomy. Claude Lévi-Strauss was an eminent French anthropologist who founded structural anthropology, influencing structuralist literary theory rather than New Criticism.

items.title: Q20 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Who among the following is credited with ending the system of patronage with his “Letter to Lord Chesterfield”?
items.explanation: In February 1755, Samuel Johnson addressed his celebrated open letter to Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield, rebuking the nobleman for attempting to pose as the patron of Johnson's Dictionary after withholding support during its seven years of compilation. This famous letter is widely regarded in literary history as a declaration of authorial independence that ended the tradition of aristocratic patronage.

items.title: Q21 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Who among the following illustrated the works of Thomas Gray and Robert Blair?
items.explanation: William Blake was a master engraver, painter, and visionary poet who produced 116 watercolor illustrations for Thomas Gray's Poems (commissioned in 1797) and celebrated engraved designs for Robert Blair's poem The Grave (published in 1808).

items.explanation: India achieved independence in 1947. Among R. K. Narayan's novels, Swami and Friends (1935), The Dark Room (1938), and The English Teacher (1945) appeared before independence, whereas The Financial Expert (1952) and The Guide (1958) were published after independence (C and E).

items.explanation: Edmund Spenser composed the epic allegorical poem The Faerie Queene (1590) (A-III); Philip Sidney wrote the critical treatise The Defense of Poesy (published 1595) (B-IV); Sir Thomas Wyatt wrote the Petrarchan sonnet adaptation "Whoso List to Hunt" (C-I); and Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, composed the reflective Windsor elegy "So Cruel Prison how could Betide" (D-II). This gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

items.title: Q26 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories and Pedagogy
items.stem: The Grammar Translation Method in English Language Teaching stresses on:
items.explanation: The Grammar Translation Method focuses on prescriptive grammatical rules, rote vocabulary memorization, and word-for-word translation between the native and target languages. As a result, it prioritizes strict grammatical accuracy over oral fluency or communicative appropriateness.

items.title: Q27 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories and Pedagogy
items.stem:
Identify the correct statement on about ‘Langue’ and ‘Parole’ below:
A. Langue is the abstract language system, the grammar of a language.
B. Parole is the language actually produced by its users following Langue.
C. Langue is the language actually produced by its users following Parole.
D. Parole is the abstract language system, the grammar of a system.
E. Langue and Parole are not related to one language as concepts.
items.explanation: In Ferdinand de Saussure's structural linguistics (Course in General Linguistics, 1916), langue denotes the abstract, shared grammatical system and social conventions of a language (A), while parole refers to the concrete, individual acts of speech and utterances produced by speakers within that system (B). Thus, statements A and B are correct.

items.title: Q28 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
In which of the texts, the following lines occur?
“Of all the causes which conspire to blind
Man’s erring judgement, and misguide the mind,
What the weak head with strongest bias rules,
Is pride, the never failing vice of fools.”
items.explanation: These lines appear in Part II (lines 201–204) of Alexander Pope's An Essay on Criticism (1711), where Pope warns that intellectual vanity and pride are the primary causes that mislead critics and blind their literary judgment.

items.title: Q29 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)

items.explanation: Russian Formalist Viktor Shklovsky introduced defamiliarization (ostranenie) in "Art as Technique" (1917) (A-III); Sigmund Freud theorized the uncanny (Das Unheimliche) in 1919 (B-IV); sociologist Bruno Latour co-developed Actor-Network Theory (ANT) (C-II); and Italian philosopher Giorgio Agamben wrote Homo Sacer: Sovereign Power and Bare Life (1995) (D-I). This matches A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

items.title: Q33 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem:
Which of the following novels deal with the theme of apartheid?
A. Purple Hibiscus
B. July’s People
C. Cry, the Beloved Country
D. The Mimic Men
E. My Son’s Story
items.explanation: Nadine Gordimer's July's People (1981) and My Son's Story (1990), alongside Alan Paton's Cry, the Beloved Country (1948), are set in South Africa and directly confront the racial injustice, political violence, and social trauma of apartheid (B, C, and E). In contrast, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's Purple Hibiscus is set in postcolonial Nigeria, and V. S. Naipaul's The Mimic Men explores Caribbean postcolonial displacement in London.

items.title: Q34 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Which of the following is not correctly matched?
items.explanation: Seamus Heaney wrote the famous opening poem "Digging" in Death of a Naturalist (1966); Audre Lorde published the iconic Black feminist poem "Coal" (1968); and Dom Moraes published "Kanheri Caves" in his Hawthornden Prize-winning debut A Beginning (1957). John Updike is primarily renowned for his Rabbit novels and humorous verse, whereas canonical poems titled "The Swan" were composed by Charles Baudelaire ("Le Cygne") and Rainer Maria Rilke.

items.title: Q35 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem: Which of the following is an elegy on John Donne’s wife who died in 1617?
items.explanation: John Donne's wife, Ann More, passed away on August 15, 1617, at the age of thirty-three. Donne mourned her loss in "Holy Sonnet XVII" ("Since she whom I lov'd hath paid her last debt / To Nature, and to hers, and my good is dead"), converting his marital grief into an intensified spiritual devotion to God.

items.title: Q36 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)

A. Deconstruction and Criticism
B. Multiculturalism: Roots and Realities
C. Literary Theory and the Claims of History
D. The Western Canon
E. An Appetite for Poetry
items.explanation: The publication years of these theoretical works in chronological order are: Deconstruction and Criticism by Harold Bloom, Paul de Man, Jacques Derrida, Geoffrey Hartman, and J. Hillis Miller (1979), Frank Kermode's An Appetite for Poetry (1989), Harold Bloom's The Western Canon (1994), Satya P. Mohanty's Literary Theory and the Claims of History (1997), and C. James Trotman's Multiculturalism: Roots and Realities (2002). This sequence is A -> E -> D -> C -> B.

items.title: Q37 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem: Which of the following novelists did not employ “Stream of Consciousness” technique?
items.explanation: Virginia Woolf (Mrs Dalloway), James Joyce (Ulysses), and Dorothy Richardson (Pilgrimage) are pioneering modernists who famously deployed the stream-of-consciousness technique to capture internal human consciousness. Graham Greene wrote realistic psychological novels and Catholic moral thrillers without utilizing stream of consciousness.

items.title: Q38 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem:
Arrange the following works of Francis Bacon in the chronological order of their year of publication:
A. Advancement of Learning
B. De Augmentis Scientiarum
C. Novum Organum
D. The New Atlantis
E. History of Henry VII
items.explanation: Francis Bacon's works in chronological order of publication are: The Advancement of Learning (1605), Novum Organum (1620), The History of Henry VII (1622), De Augmentis Scientiarum (the expanded Latin edition, 1623), and the posthumously published utopian text The New Atlantis (1627). This sequence corresponds to A -> C -> E -> B -> D.

items.title: Q39 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem: The author of “The Politics of Translation” and translator of Mahashweta Devi’s “Standayini” is:
items.explanation: Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak translated Mahasweta Devi's Bengali short story "Standayini" as "Breast-Giver" (in In Other Worlds, 1987) and authored the seminal essay "The Politics of Translation" (published in Outside in the Teaching Machine, 1993), analyzing translation as an intimate, ethical, and political act.

items.title: Q40 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about Modernism?
A. Modernism marked a break with formal conventions
B. Old ways of thought underwent cultural shift
C. Decline of liberal humanism
D. Modernism revived classical scholarship
E. Modernism promoted logocentric way of thoughts
items.explanation: Modernism was defined by a radical aesthetic departure from 19th-century realism and Victorian conventions (A), a profound cultural shift following industrialization and psychological insights (B), and widespread skepticism toward liberal humanist assumptions of inevitable progress after World War I (C). Statements D and E are incorrect because Modernism did not seek to restore classical scholarship nor advocate logocentric thought.

items.title: Q41 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem: Langston Hughes’ poem “I too Sing America” is a response to which of the following poets?
items.explanation: Langston Hughes composed "I, Too" ("I, too, sing America") in 1926 as a direct dialogue with and critique of Walt Whitman's patriotic anthem "I Hear America Singing" (1860). Hughes asserts that African Americans are an integral, beautiful, and equal part of the American nation who claim their rightful place at the table.

items.title: Q42 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem:
Choose the correct sequence of the following works of Pablo Neruda in chronological order:-
A. Spain in the Heart
B. Works and Book of Twilights
C. The Inhabitant and His Hope
D. Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair
E. The Trying of Infinite Man
items.explanation: The chronological order of Pablo Neruda's early works is: Crepusculario (Book of Twilights, 1923), Veinte poemas de amor y una canción desesperada (Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair, 1924), Tentativa del hombre infinito (The Trying of Infinite Man, 1926), El habitante y su esperanza (The Inhabitant and His Hope, 1926), and his Spanish Civil War volume España en el corazón (Spain in the Heart, 1937). This sequence corresponds to B -> D -> E -> C -> A.

items.title: Q43 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem:
Arrange the following poems by W. B. Yeats in the chronological order of their year of publication:
A. “Adam’s Curse”
B. “Among School Children”
C. “The Second Coming”
D. “The Wild Swans at Coole”
E. “Under Ben Bulben”
items.explanation: The chronological order of W. B. Yeats's poems by publication year is: "Adam's Curse" (In the Seven Woods, 1903), "The Wild Swans at Coole" (1917), "The Second Coming" (1920/1921), "Among School Children" (The Tower, 1928), and his final poetic testament "Under Ben Bulben" (1938/1939). This sequence is A -> D -> C -> B -> E.

items.title: Q44 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Match the column:
(Author)
A. Manohar Malgaonkar
B. Chaman Nahal
C. Ruskin Bond
D. Arun Joshi
(Text)
I. The Weird Dance and Other Stories
II. The Survivor
III. Rumble Tumble
IV. Neighbour’s Wife and Other Stories
items.explanation: Manohar Malgonkar published the story collection Rumble-Tumble (1977) (A-III); Chaman Nahal wrote The Weird Dance and Other Stories (1965) (B-I); Ruskin Bond authored The Neighbour's Wife and Other Stories (1967) (C-IV); and Arun Joshi published The Survivor and Other Stories (1975) (D-II). This gives A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

items.title: Q45 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem:
“Success is counted sweetest
By those who ne’er succeed.
To comprehend a nectar
Requires sorest need.”
Who has composed the above lines?
items.explanation: These are the opening stanzas of Emily Dickinson's poem "Success is counted sweetest" (written c. 1859, published 1864), which expresses the paradox that victory is comprehended most keenly by those who experience defeat.

items.title: Q46 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VII: Cultural Studies
items.stem:
Which of the statements given below are true?
A. The centre for contemporary Cultural Studies was established in Berkley in 1960.
B. Jurgen Habermas traces the rise of the public sphere to the rise of print culture.
C. Paul Gilroy introduced the concept of the Black Atlantic.
D. Adorno praises the alien nature of avant-garde modernist art such as the atonal music of Schoenberg.
E. Chutnification was a term used by Edward Soja.
items.explanation: Statements B, C, and D are true: Jürgen Habermas linked the emergence of the bourgeois public sphere to print capitalism and periodicals; Paul Gilroy theorized the "Black Atlantic" (1993); and Theodor Adorno praised Arnold Schoenberg's difficult atonal compositions for resisting culture-industry commodification. Statement A is false because the Centre for Contemporary Cultural Studies (CCCS) was founded in 1964 at the University of Birmingham, and statement E is false because "chutnification" is a term coined by Salman Rushdie in Midnight's Children (1981).

items.title: Q47 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: When was ‘International Phonetic Alphabet’ (IPA) developed and promulgated?
items.explanation: The International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) was first developed and promulgated in August 1888 by the International Phonetic Association (founded in Paris in 1886 by Paul Passy) to establish a standardized phonetic representation for all spoken languages.

items.title: Q48 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true about A. K. Ramanujan?
A. He is a poet of the sixties.
B. His poetry draws his sustenance from his awareness of Hindu heritage.
C. He has poor sense of rhythm.
D. His verse poorly utilises Akam constructed techniques.
E. He utilises Akam constructed techniques in his poetry.
items.explanation: Statements A, B, and E are true: A. K. Ramanujan emerged as a leading poet of the 1960s with The Striders (1966), drew rich thematic sustenance from his South Indian Hindu heritage, and skillfully integrated the interiorized conventions of classical Tamil akam poetry into his modern English verse. Statements C and D are false because Ramanujan is universally praised for his subtle, disciplined rhythmic craftsmanship.

items.title: Q49 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem:
Arrange the following novels of D. H. Lawrence in chronological order of their year of publication:-
A. Women in Love
B. The White Peacock
C. Sons and Lovers
D. The Rainbow
E. The Trespasser
items.explanation: D. H. Lawrence's novels in chronological order of publication are: The White Peacock (1911), The Trespasser (1912), Sons and Lovers (1913), The Rainbow (1915), and Women in Love (1920). This sequence corresponds to B -> E -> C -> D -> A.

items.title: Q50 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem:
Identify the correct options from the following statements:
A. Ecocriticism has often explained the ‘human and non-human webs of interrelation.”
B. In Ecocriticism, human accountability to the environment is part of the text’s ethical orientation.
C. Ecocriticism foregrounds the notion of an interplay between environment and the body.
D. There is only one wave of Ecocriticism.
E. Ecocriticism has not tackled the issue of gender.
items.explanation: Statements A, B, and C capture foundational principles of ecocriticism: the interconnectedness of human and non-human worlds, ecological accountability as a central ethical orientation, and the physical interplay between human bodies and natural environments. Statement D is false because ecocriticism has developed across multiple distinct waves, and statement E is false because ecofeminism is a foundational branch of ecocritical inquiry.

items.title: Q51 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: In which year was Raja Rao’s Kanthapura published?
items.explanation: Raja Rao's landmark debut novel Kanthapura, recounting the impact of Mahatma Gandhi's nonviolent struggle on a South Indian village through the vernacular sthala-purana storytelling style of the elder Achakka, was published in London in 1938.

items.title: Q52 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Identify all the Australian Aboriginal writers out of the following:
A. Kim Scott
B. Peter Carey
C. Oodgeroo Noonuccal
D. Kevin Gilbert
E. Derek Walcott
items.explanation: Kim Scott (Noongar novelist and Miles Franklin winner), Oodgeroo Noonuccal (Kath Walker, pioneering poet of We Are Going), and Kevin Gilbert (Wiradjuri poet, playwright, and activist) are Indigenous Australian Aboriginal writers (A, C, and D). In contrast, Peter Carey is a white Australian writer, and Derek Walcott was a Nobel laureate from Saint Lucia in the Caribbean.

items.title: Q53 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Renaissance, Elizabethan & Jacobean Age · Unit I: Drama
items.stem: Which of the following is a Dramatic Monologue?
items.explanation: Robert Browning's "Andrea del Sarto" (published in Men and Women, 1855) is an iconic Victorian dramatic monologue in which the Renaissance painter addresses his silent wife Lucrezia in blank verse, revealing his artistic compromises, emotional dependence, and psychological melancholy.

items.title: Q54 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Which of the following texts has been written by Rabindranath Tagore?
items.explanation: Chandalika (1938) is a celebrated dance-drama by Rabindranath Tagore, based on the Buddhist legend of Prakriti, an untouchable young woman who falls in love with the monk Ananda, offering a profound critique of caste prejudice and spiritual rebirth.

items.title: Q55 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Match the column:
A. The Golden Light
B. The Lotus
C. Indian Dancers
D. The Harp of India
I. Toru Dutt
II. Sarojini Naidu
III. Henry Derozio
IV. Sri Aurobindo
items.explanation: Sri Aurobindo wrote the spiritual sonnet "The Golden Light" (A-IV); Toru Dutt composed the Petrarchan sonnet "The Lotus" in Ancient Ballads and Legends of Hindustan (1882) (B-I); Sarojini Naidu wrote "Indian Dancers" in The Golden Threshold (1905) (C-II); and Henry Louis Vivian Derozio wrote the patriotic sonnet "The Harp of India" in Poems (1827) (D-III). This gives A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

items.title: Q56 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Arrange the following works in the chronological order of their year of publication:
A. S. Menon Marath’s The Wound of Spring
B. Humayun Kabir’s Men and Rivers
C. Anand Lall’s The House at Adampur
D. Sudhindra N. Ghose’s The Vermillion Boat
E. Ved Mehta’s Delinquent Chacha
items.explanation: The chronological sequence of these Indian English works is: Humayun Kabir's Men and Rivers (1945), Sudhindra Nath Ghose's The Vermilion Boat (1953), Arthur S. Lall's The House at Adampur (1956), S. Menon Marath's The Wound of Spring (1960), and Ved Mehta's Delinquent Chacha (1966). This forms the sequence B -> D -> C -> A -> E.

items.title: Q57 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Renaissance, Elizabethan & Jacobean Age · Unit I: Drama
items.stem: The first folio of Shakespeare’s plays appeared in:
items.explanation: The First Folio of William Shakespeare's dramatic works, titled Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies, was prepared and published by his fellow King's Men actors John Heminges and Henry Condell in 1623.

items.title: Q58 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Who is the best known figure amongst the following for articulating the concept of ‘Negritude’?
items.explanation: Martinican poet and statesman Aimé Césaire coined and articulated the concept of Négritude in the 1930s (most prominently in Cahier d'un retour au pays natal, 1939) alongside Léopold Sédar Senghor and Léon Damas, creating a literary movement that celebrated Black African cultural heritage and resisted French colonial assimilation.

items.title: Q59 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem: Which of the following poems uses ‘terza rima’?
options: P. B. Shelley’s “Ode to the West Wind”
items.explanation: P. B. Shelley's "Ode to the West Wind" (1820) is written in five fourteen-line sections composed in Dantean terza rima (aba bcb cdc ded ee), using interlocking three-line tercets linked by rhyme and resolved in a final couplet.

items.title: Q60 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem:
From which poem are the following lines extracted?
“Once more the storm is howling and half hid
Under this cradle-hood and coverlid,
My child sleeps on. There is no obstacle.
But Gregory’s wood and one bare hill.”
items.explanation: These are the opening lines of W. B. Yeats's poem "A Prayer for My Daughter" (composed in 1919 and published in Michael Robartes and the Dancer, 1921), written at Thoor Ballylee as he meditates on his sleeping daughter Anne while a fierce storm rages across the Irish countryside.

items.title: Q61 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem: Which among the following is the last novel of George Eliot?
items.explanation: Daniel Deronda, published in 1876, is George Eliot's eighth and final completed novel, contrasting the social world of upper-class Victorian England with a serious exploration of Jewish heritage and proto-Zionist themes.

items.title: Q62 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Romantic Period · Unit II: Poetry
items.stem: The famous short poem “Elegy on the Death of a Mad Dog” appears in which one of the following Eighteenth Century novels?
options: The Vicar of Wakefield by Oliver Goldsmith
The Castle of Otranto by Horace Walpole
items.explanation: Oliver Goldsmith's satirical mock-elegy "An Elegy on the Death of a Mad Dog" (famous for its comic climax where "the man recover'd of the bite, / The dog it was that dy'd") is recited in Chapter 17 of Goldsmith's novel The Vicar of Wakefield (1766).

items.title: Q63 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Which of the following is not an autobiography?
items.explanation: Patrick White: A Life (1991) is a biography of the Australian Nobel laureate written by biographer David Marr. In contrast, Nelson Mandela's Long Walk to Freedom (1994), M. K. Gandhi's The Story of My Experiments with Truth (1927), and Sharankumar Limbale's The Outcaste: Akkarmashi (1984) are all autobiographies.

items.title: Q64 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem:
Arrange the following works in the chronological sequence of their year of publication:
A. Matthew Arnold’s Culture and Anarchy
B. Robert Burton’s The Anatomy of Melancholy
C. P. B. Shelley’s Defence of Poetry
D. Thomas Hobbes’ Leviathan
E. Walter Pater’s Studies in the History of the Renaissance
items.explanation: The chronological order is: Robert Burton's The Anatomy of Melancholy (1621), Thomas Hobbes's Leviathan (1651), P. B. Shelley's A Defence of Poetry (written 1821, published 1840), Matthew Arnold's Culture and Anarchy (1869), and Walter Pater's Studies in the History of the Renaissance (1873). This yields the sequence B -> D -> C -> A -> E.

items.title: Q65 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: What does deductive method of reasoning refer to?
items.explanation: Deductive reasoning is a top-down logical approach that begins with general premises or overarching principles and deduces logically necessary conclusions about specific, particular cases. Inductive reasoning, by contrast, moves from specific empirical observations to general conclusions.

items.title: Q66 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of their year of publication:
A. “The Tyger”
B. “The Solitary Reaper”
C. “Adonais”
D. “The Rime of the Ancient Mariner”
E. “Ode to Autumn”
items.explanation: The publication dates of these Romantic poems in chronological order are: William Blake's "The Tyger" (Songs of Experience, 1794), S. T. Coleridge's "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner" (Lyrical Ballads, 1798), William Wordsworth's "The Solitary Reaper" (Poems, in Two Volumes, 1807), John Keats's "To Autumn" (1820), and P. B. Shelley's elegy "Adonais" (1821). This corresponds to A -> D -> B -> E -> C.

items.title: Q67 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Which of the following is not a character in William Congreve’s The Way of the World?
items.explanation: Mirabell, Edward Fainall, and Waitwell are central characters in William Congreve's Restoration comedy of manners The Way of the World (1700). Peachum is the dishonest fence and receiver of stolen goods in John Gay's satirical ballad opera The Beggar's Opera (1728).

items.title: Q68 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
“O Sir, content you’,
I follow him to serve my turn upon him.
We cannot all be masters, nor all masters cannot be truly followed.”
The above lines were spoken by which of the following characters?
items.explanation: These lines are spoken by Iago to Roderigo in the opening scene of William Shakespeare's Othello (Act 1, Scene 1), where Iago candidly reveals that his apparent devotion to Othello is merely a deceitful facade to engineer his personal revenge.

items.title: Q69 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their year of publication:
A. Fraser’s Magazine
B. The Spectator
C. The Westminster Review
D. The Quarterly Review
E. Edinburgh Review
items.explanation: The founding dates of these British periodicals in chronological order are: The Edinburgh Review (founded 1802), the Tory periodical The Quarterly Review (founded 1809), the utilitarian Westminster Review (founded 1824), the weekly journal The Spectator (founded 1828), and Fraser's Magazine (founded 1830). This establishes the sequence E -> D -> C -> B -> A.

items.title: Q70 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose

Match the column:
A. My Days with Gandhi
B. Among the Great
C. Life of Sri Aurobindo
D. Rabindranath Tagore
I. D.K. Roy
II. N.K. Basu
III. Krishna Kripalani
IV. A.B. Purani
items.explanation: Nirmal Kumar Bose (N. K. Basu) wrote the personal memoir My Days with Gandhi (1953) (A-II); Dilip Kumar Roy authored Among the Great (1947), recording intimate conversations with Gandhi, Sri Aurobindo, and Tagore (B-I); Ambalal Balkrishna Purani authored The Life of Sri Aurobindo (1958) (C-IV); and Krishna Kripalani authored the biography Rabindranath Tagore: A Biography (1962) (D-III). This gives A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

items.title: Q71 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem:
Match the column:
(Term)
A. Antonomasia
B. Antiphrasis
C. Apocrypha
D. Aretalogy
(Meaning)
I. Writings or statements of doubtful or spurious authorship.
II. A figure of speech in which some defining word or phrase is substituted for a person’s proper name.
III. A narrative of miraculous deeds of God or Hero.
IV. Ironic or humorous use of words in senses opposite to the generally accepted meanings.
items.explanation: Antonomasia substitutes an epithet or descriptive title for a proper name, like calling Aristotle "The Stagirite" (A-II); Antiphrasis uses words in senses directly opposite to their literal meaning for irony (B-IV); Apocrypha refers to texts of uncertain, questionable, or spurious authorship (C-I); and Aretalogy denotes a sacred narrative recounting the miraculous deeds and virtues of a god or hero (D-III). This matches A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

items.title: Q72 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods and Materials in English
items.stem:
Which of the following are correct according to the MLA Handbook, 9th edition?
A. One inch margin on all sides is compulsory in a research page.
B. Co-ordinating conjunctions are written in bold letters in the title of a research paper.
C. Slash is used between two nouns paired as opposites.
D. Hanging indent in the works cited entry is ½ inches
E. Subordinating conjunctions are not written in bold letters in the title of the research paper.
items.explanation: According to the MLA Handbook (9th edition), page margins must be exactly 1 inch on all four sides (A), a forward slash without spaces is used to join paired contrasting or alternative nouns (C), and entries in the Works Cited list must use a hanging indent of 0.5 inches (½ inch) (D). Statements B and E are incorrect because paper titles in MLA style are never formatted in bold font.

items.title: Q73 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Victorian Period · Unit III: Fiction & Short Story
items.stem:
Identify the statements which are true for Psychoanalytic Criticism.
A. The premises and procedures were established by Sigmund Freud.
B. Freud posited that artists are like neurotic patients.
C. Freud posited that ‘Psychoanalysis’ can be used to account for many developments and practices in the history of civilization.
D. A repressed wish does not become fantasy.
E. Freud proposed that literature and other arts manifest the repressed subconscious and unconscious drives of the artist.
items.explanation: Statements A, C, and E are true: psychoanalytic criticism is grounded in the foundational concepts of Sigmund Freud (A), Freud applied psychoanalysis to interpret societal rituals and cultural institutions in works like Civilization and Its Discontents (C), and psychoanalytic theory views literature as an indirect expression and sublimation of unconscious drives (E). Statement D is false because Freud specifically showed that repressed wishes give rise to daydreams and fantasies.

items.title: Q74 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Renaissance, Elizabethan & Jacobean Age · Unit I: Drama
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are correct about ‘Litotes’?
A. It contains an understatement for emphasis.
B. It is not opposite of hyperbole.
C. It is used with laconic intentions.
D. It is used with ironic intentions.
E. It is used in dramatic context.
items.explanation: Litotes is a figure of speech featuring intentional understatement achieved by negating the opposite (such as "he was not unhappy") (A), often chosen for its laconic restraint (C) and understated, ironic wit (D). Statement B is incorrect because litotes is precisely the rhetorical opposite of hyperbole (overstatement).

items.title: Q75 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit VI: English in India: History, Evolution and Futures
items.stem: Who is the author of English in India : Its Present and Future published in 1964?
items.explanation: Vinayak Krishna Gokak (V. K. Gokak), the eminent Kannada scholar, writer, and educationist, wrote English in India: Its Present and Future (1964), an influential assessment of English language pedagogy and language policy in post-colonial India.

items.title: Q76 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Renaissance, Elizabethan & Jacobean Age · Unit I: Drama
items.stem: Shakespeare’s Much Ado About Nothing is a:
items.explanation: Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing (c. 1598) is a classic romantic comedy centered on the witty "merry war" and mutual courtship of Beatrice and Benedick, alongside the romantic melodrama and eventual wedding of Hero and Claudio.

items.title: Q77 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods and Materials in English
items.stem:
An ideal research paper should include:
A. A statement that establishes the problem or controversial issue that the paper intends to examine.
B. Background information to establish past theories and current ideas on the topic.
C. Summarizing and paraphrasing.
D. Glorification of the paper writer himself.
E. A thesis to establish one’s position.
items.explanation: A sound academic research paper requires a clear statement of the research problem or question (A), sufficient literature review and background context to frame current scholarly debates (B), and a clear, argumentative thesis statement establishing the author's claim (E). Self-glorification (D) violates scholarly objectivity, while summarization (C) is merely a supporting technique rather than a foundational requirement.

items.title: Q78 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem: Who said “The introduction of foreigners does not necessarily destroy the nation, they merge in it”?
items.explanation: In Hind Swaraj (1909), Chapter 10 ("The Condition of India: The Hindus and the Mahomedans"), Mahatma Gandhi argued for an inclusive concept of Indian nationhood, stating that India has historically assimilated diverse populations and that "The introduction of foreigners does not necessarily destroy the nation, they merge in it."

items.title: Q79 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Units V–X: Language, English in India, Cultural Studies, Criticism, Theory & Research · Unit X: Research Methods and Materials in English
items.stem:
The incorrect works cited entries according to MLA Handbook, 9th edition are:
A. Jacobs, Alan. The Pleasures of Reading in the Age of Destruction. Oxford UP, 2011.
B. Charon, Rita, et al. The Principles and Practice of Narrative Medicine. Oxford UP, London, 2017.
C. Sabau, Ana. “The Perils of Ownership.” American Review, vol. 10, no. 2, 2007, pp. 1-27.
D. Riddle, Julie. “Shadow Animals.” The Georgia Review, 67.3, pp. 424-47.
E. Copeland, Edward. The Cambridge Companion to Jane Austen. Cambridge UP, 1997. 131-48.
items.explanation: In MLA 9th edition: entry B incorrectly includes the city of publication ("London"), which is obsolete for modern books; entry D formats volume and issue as "67.3" instead of the required "vol. 67, no. 3"; and entry E omits the required "pp." prefix before page numbers and omits chapter/contributor details for an edited collection. Entries A and C follow correct MLA 9 guidelines.

items.title: Q80 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Literary Criticism & Theory · Unit VIII: Literary Criticism
items.stem:
Identify the poet who has composed the following lines:
“Ganga was sunken, and the limp leaves
Waited for rain, while the black clouds
Gathered far distant, over Himavant.
The Jungle crouched, humped in silence.”
items.explanation: These lines appear in Part V ("What the Thunder Said", lines 395–398) of T. S. Eliot's landmark modernist poem The Waste Land (1922), setting a parched Indian drought scene before the voice of the thunder utters the Upanishadic message "Datta, Dayadhvam, Damyata."

items.title: Q81 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Match the column:
A. Henry Miller
B. John Steinbeck
C. James Jones
D. James Baldwin
I. The Grapes of Wrath
II. No Name in the Street
III. Tropic of Cancer
IV. From Here to Eternity
items.explanation: Henry Miller wrote Tropic of Cancer (1934) (A-III); John Steinbeck wrote the Pulitzer Prize-winning novel The Grapes of Wrath (1939) (B-I); James Jones wrote the World War II novel From Here to Eternity (1951) (C-IV); and James Baldwin authored the civil rights essay collection No Name in the Street (1972) (D-II). This gives A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

items.title: Q82 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)
items.meta: Modernist & Early 20th Century · Unit IV: Non-Fictional Prose
items.stem:
Which of the following options are true about the epistemological dimension of research?
A. Scientific realism
B. The search for truth
C. Critical theory
D. Certain and indubitable knowledge
E. Mechanism of social control
items.explanation: Epistemology is the branch of philosophy that examines the nature, origin, and limits of human knowledge. Within research methodology, its primary focus is on the systematic search for truth (B) and establishing the validity criteria through which knowledge can be considered certain and indubitable (D).

items.title: Q83 · Jan 2025 (Shift 2 - Dec 2024 Cycle)

items.stem:
[Reading Comprehension: Prose Passage]
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:

"One key development in the evolving discussion surrounding popular culture which occurred during the early twentieth century was the association of popular culture with the United States of America. Through Hollywood and associated modes of popular entertainment, USA was beginning to exercise international cultural influence. The term 'Mass culture' is particularly relevant in this context as it refers to both the effects of American culture as well as to a specific theoretical debate that emerged in America during the post-war period. Dominic Strinati contends in his An Introduction to Theories of Popular Culture (1995) that 'mass culture refers to popular culture which is produced by the industrial techniques of mass production, and marketed for profit to a mass public of consumers.' Such a view of popular culture argues that the industrial revolution produces a series of atomised individuals who had not only lost touch with the communities of shared interest to which they once belonged but that they had also been subjected to the process of mechanisation and alienation. This rendered them ripe for systematic cultural manipulation through uniform, mass produced formulaic products designed to evoke frivolous, escapist and superficial pleasures."

Question:
Systematic culture manipulation takes place through:
items.explanation: According to Dominic Strinati's argument in the passage, industrial mass production creates "atomised individuals" who become vulnerable to "systematic cultural manipulation through uniform, mass produced formulaic products," which he defines as mass culture. Thus, systematic cultural manipulation occurs specifically through the mass production of culture.

[Reading Comprehension: Poem]
Read the following poem carefully and answer the questions that follow:

"In all my wand'rings round this world of care,
In all my griefs—and God has giv'n my share—
I still had hopes my latest hours to crown,
Amidst these humble bow'rs to lay me down;
To husband out life's taper at the close,
And keep the flame from wasting by repose;
I still had hopes, for pride attends us still,
Amidst the swains to show my book-learn'd skill,
Around my fire an ev'ning group to draw,
And tell of all I felt, and all I saw."
— Oliver Goldsmith, The Deserted Village (1770)

Question:
What does the poem say about the nature of the world?
options: It’s full of care and hope
items.explanation: In the opening lines of Oliver Goldsmith's excerpt, the speaker refers to "this world of care" while repeatedly declaring "I still had hopes," depicting the world as one marked by tribulations yet sustained by enduring hope.
